comment: The observation types a requirement may name. Describes what a platform's accessibility layer exposes — not a view about design. `needs` is derived from this table, so bindings carry it only when a requirement needs more (via needs_also).

role.means: the semantic role the platform's accessibility layer reports
role.note: computed, never authored — reading a role attribute checks what someone typed

name.means: the accessible name the platform computes for the element

state.means: a state the platform exposes to assistive technology

order.means: the sequence of children as the platform reports them

containment.means: whether one element is within another's subtree

focus.means: whether an element participates in sequential focus, and where focus is

announcement.means: something spoken by assistive technology without focus moving

event.means: a callback, signal or notification the component emits or receives

layout.note: a relation the contract states, never an appearance judgment

token.means: whether a value resolved through a named design token
token.note: data-flow only — not that the value is correct, which is visual regression's job
